title: Union Ministers Smt. Annpurna Devi and Shri Jayant Chaudhary launch NAVYA 2.0 in Haridwar
subtitle:
NAVYA 2.0 to Cover 100 Districts Across 24 States and UTs; Eligibility Widened to 16–25 Years with End-to-End Tracking via Skill India Digital Hub
477 Saksham Anganwadi Centres and Five New PM-JANMAN Anganwadi Centres Inaugurated in Uttarakhand; 10 PMKVY 4.0 Trainees Felicitated
body_text: Smt. Annpurna Devi, Union Minister for Women and Child Development, and Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, jointly launched NAVYA 2.0 from Uttarakhand Sanskrit Sansthanam in Haridwar. NAVYA, Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Women and Adolescent Girls, is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Women and Child Development and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. NAVYA 2.0 will cover 100 districts across 24 States and Union Territories, with a focus on aspirational and hard-to-reach areas. It widens eligibility from 16–18 years to 16–25 years and offers training in industry-relevant, emerging and non-traditional job roles, with pathways to employment, apprenticeships and entrepreneurship. A common Standard Operating Procedure will guide district-level implementation, while the Skill India Digital Hub will support candidates from enrolment to certification and track their training progress. Speaking at the occasion, Smt. Annpurna Devi, Minister for Women and Child Development, Government of India, said, “Maa Ganga's eternal flow reminds us to keep moving forward. In Haridwar, that same spirit is being realised through NAVYA 2.0. The vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 will remain incomplete without the full participation of women. They must not only be beneficiaries of development but its leaders. From our villages to outer space, our daughters have shown that when given the opportunity, they move ahead. The Government is supporting every stage of a girl's journey through a range of schemes, and NAVYA 2.0 carries this commitment forward. Mobilisation is not merely about filling training batches; it is a sustained engagement with every girl and her family, from enrolment to livelihood. With State Nodal Officers leading implementation and the SIDH portal tracking each girl's progress, we will ensure that every trained girl is placed on a path to meaningful work.” Expressing his views in his virtual message on the initiative, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, said, “The success of a skilling programme is measured by the opportunities it opens up after training. Through NAVYA 2.0, we want more young women, particularly in underserved districts, to pursue careers they may not have considered, gain practical experience through apprenticeships or start enterprises of their own. Enabling more women to join and shape India’s workforce is essential to realising our vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.” NAVYA 2.0 will expand access to training in new-age and non-traditional job roles, building on the pilot phase, which trained adolescent girls in roles such as Drone Manufacturing and Assembly Technician and Solar PV Installation Helper. By equipping young women with skills for emerging sectors and opening pathways to employment, apprenticeships and entrepreneurship, the initiative seeks to increase women’s participation in the workforce and advance the vision of women-led development for Viksit Bharat 2047. The launch programme also witnessed the inauguration of 477 Saksham Anganwadi Centres and five new Anganwadi Centres constructed under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) in Uttarakhand. Additionally, 10 candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 were felicitated. The event was also graced by Smt. Rekha Arya, Cabinet Minister for Women Empowerment and Child Development, Food and Civil Supplies, Sports and Youth Welfare, Government of Uttarakhand; Shri Madan Kaushik, Cabinet Minister of Panchayati Raj, Disaster Management and Rehabilitation, Ayush and Ayush Education, Reorganization and Census, Government of Uttarakhand; Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat, Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, Uttarakhand; Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE; Shri Anil Malik, Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development; Ms. Hena Usman, Joint Secretary, MSDE; Shri Ajeet Kumar, Joint Secretary, MWCD and other senior officials of MSDE and MWCD. The next phase of NAVYA places emphasis on what comes after training: the opportunity to apply new skills in a job, build experience through an apprenticeship or start an enterprise. By making these pathways more accessible to adolescent girls and young women, NAVYA 2.0 seeks to support their economic independence and enable more women to contribute to Viksit Bharat 2047. *** RC/SM
